review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. CDFW/UC Santa Barbara physiology and life-history sources support surf-zone temperature response and shallow sandy-beach habitat; no catch-probability curve validated.

profile.size: Min limit None / Bag limit 20 per harvester / day aggregate

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for barred surfperch.
factors.value_notes: A UC Santa Barbara study of 61 wild barred surfperch measured metabolic and cardiac performance at 12, 16, 20 and 22 °C. Aerobic performance remained relatively stable from 12-20 °C, while temperatures above 20 °C were limiting, especially for smaller young-of-year fish. This supports a thermal response but is not a field-derived SST preference or catch curve; the configured 12-21 °C range and 14-19 °C ideal are not directly calibrated.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for barred surfperch.
factors.value_notes: Barred surfperch primarily occupy the surf zone over sandy beaches; FishBase and California survey sources report shallow occurrence around 0-7 m, with trawl records to 73 m. This supports the configured 1-15 m shallow-beach screen but does not validate the 3-10 m ideal or represent all deeper incidental records.
